    Open now

    The register is open: paid work for people starting out

    Studio Canteen. Films, photographs, music, print and events, made in Glasgow with the people in them.

    What we do

    We want to make more room for local creatives in Glasgow.

    Why we exist

    A lot of talented people in Glasgow never get their first paid job. The industry still runs on who you know, and on whether you can afford to work for free.

    We think the work itself should be the way in. So we take on real client jobs and put emerging creatives on the crew, at a proper rate.

    We also make our own films and print about the city's culture. That's how most people find us, and it's how we cover the scene we're part of.

    2. 02 Put yourself forward Join the register of creatives we bring onto paid jobs. Free, no portfolio needed. One of us emails to say hello within two weeks.
    3. 03 Opportunities and workshops Free skills sessions and paid placements for people on the register. Ask us about the next one.
    4. 04 Come to an event Screenings, talks and workshops around the city. Many are free. See what's on.
    5. 05 Commission us Photography, film and creative direction for labels, artists, venues and brands. We reply with questions or a quote.
    6. 06 Support us Members fund our events and print, and get free or reduced tickets and every issue. From £3 a month.
    7. 07 Talk to one of us Not sure where to start? Write to Rowan, Kye or Wilf directly. They reply themselves.

    Home/Get involved

    For emerging creatives

    Paid creative work, for people starting out.

    Our register is the list of emerging creatives we bring onto client jobs. If you live in or around Glasgow, it's free to join.

    Ways in

    Clients pay us for commissioned work. Supporters and members fund the free side: events, print and skills sessions. People who take part never pay, and you don't need a portfolio or contacts.

    1. 01 Suggest a person or story Point us to someone in Glasgow whose work should be seen. We read every one and contact you if we take it forward.
    2. 02 Put yourself forward Join the register of creatives we bring onto paid jobs. Free, no portfolio needed. One of us emails to say hello within two weeks.
    3. 03 Opportunities and workshops Free skills sessions and paid placements for people on the register. Ask us about the next one.
    4. 04 Come to an event Screenings, talks and workshops around the city. Many are free. See what's on.
    5. 05 Commission us Photography, film and creative direction for labels, artists, venues and brands. We reply with questions or a quote.
    6. 06 Support us Members fund our events and print, and get free or reduced tickets and every issue. From £3 a month.
    7. 07 Talk to one of us Not sure where to start? Write to Rowan, Kye or Wilf directly. They reply themselves.

    Who it's for

    Young Glasgow creatives, and anyone who has found it hard to get a start because of money.

    You don't need an agent or a finished portfolio. You need to be good at something and keen to do it properly.

    What we offer

    1. 01 The register Tell us what you do. When a job suits you, we'll send the details and the fee.
    2. 02 Paid placements A paid place on a client job, working alongside Rowan, Kye or Wilf from brief to delivery.
    3. 03 Skills sessions Free, practical sessions for everyone on the register.

    Join the register

    Four questions. We'll only contact you about work, placements and skills sessions.

    Why we ask: your postcode tells us you're local, and your discipline helps us match you to the right job. After you join, one of us will email to say hello within two weeks.

    Not a creative yourself? Support our work.

    Suggest a person or story

    Know someone in Glasgow whose work more people should see? An artist, musician, maker, a venue, a night, a project. Tell us about them.

    Why we ask: your email is only so we can ask a follow-up question. We will check with the person before featuring them.

    We read every suggestion. If we take it forward, we will contact you and then them.

    Talk to one of us

    Not sure which form is right, or would rather just ask? Write to one of us directly.

    Why we ask: we need your email to reply. Nothing else is required.

    The person you choose will reply themselves, usually within a week.

    Home/About

    About Studio Canteen

    We make the work we cover.

    Studio Canteen is a media, community and culture collective in Glasgow, run by Rowan Syed-Tollan, Kye O'Hagan and Wilf Pearce. We take on commercial creative work, bring emerging local creatives onto it, and pay them properly.

    Why we exist

    A lot of talented people in Glasgow never get their first paid job. The industry still runs on who you know, and on whether you can afford to work for free.

    We think the work itself should be the way in. So we take on real client jobs and put emerging creatives on the crew, at a proper rate.

    We also make our own films and print about the city's culture. That's how most people find us, and it's how we cover the scene we're part of.

    Our goals

    1. 01 More paid opportunities Bring more emerging Glasgow creatives onto real jobs, at a proper rate.
    2. 02 Free skills Run regular free sessions on the parts of the job nobody teaches you.
    3. 03 Cover our own scene Keep making independent films and print about Glasgow's culture.

    How the work is funded

    When you commission us, most of the fee goes to the creatives who make the work.

    We keep a small share to run the studio. It pays for paid placements, free skills sessions and our own films and print.

    Home/Accessibility statement

    Accessibility

    Accessibility statement

    We want everyone to be able to use this website, whatever their device, ability or way of browsing.

    Last updated

    October 2026

    Questions

    business@studiocanteen.com

    Our standard

    We aim to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at level AA. These guidelines explain how to make web content easier to use for people with disabilities, and for everyone else.

    What you can do on this site

    • Move through every page, menu, filter and form using a keyboard alone. A visible outline shows where you are.
    • Use a screen reader. Pages have a clear heading structure, landmarks and breadcrumbs, and images have text descriptions.
    • Zoom to 400% without text being cut off or the page scrolling sideways.
    • Turn off motion. If your device is set to reduce motion, the site does too.
    • Read text with strong contrast against its background, including on our colour sections.

    Video and audio

    Our films have playback controls you can use with a keyboard. Every film we publish will have captions and a transcript. If one you need is missing, email us and we will send it.

    Known issues

    We are not aware of any accessibility problems with the current site. As we add projects, films and events, we will list any known issues here.

    At our events

    When events are announced, each listing will include access information for the venue, including step-free routes, toilets, seating and whether captioning or BSL is available. If you have access needs that are not covered, contact us before the event and we will do what we can.

    Tell us about a problem

    If something on this site does not work for you, or you need information in a different format such as large print or plain text, email business@studiocanteen.com. We aim to reply within five working days.

    If you are not happy with our response

    You can contact the Equality Advisory and Support Service, which handles enquiries about accessibility in Scotland, England and Wales.

    How we tested this site

    This statement was prepared in October 2026. The site was built to WCAG 2.2 AA with keyboard navigation, visible focus, reduced-motion support and accessible colour contrast. We will review this statement after each major update, and at least once a year.

    Home/Privacy

    Privacy

    Privacy notice

    This notice explains what personal information Studio Canteen collects, why we collect it and what we do with it.

    Last updated

    October 2026

    Questions

    business@studiocanteen.com

    Who we are

    Studio Canteen is a Community Interest Company registered in Scotland. We are the data controller for the information you give us through this website. You can contact us at business@studiocanteen.com.

    What we collect

    • Newsletter. Your email address, if you sign up.
    • Book us enquiries. Your name, email, organisation and the details of your project.
    • Creative register. Your name, contact details, disciplines, location and any links or work you share with us.
    • Support us. Your name, email and the amount you choose to give. When we start taking payments, cards will be handled by a specialist payment provider, named here. We will never see or store your card details.
    • Website security. When you send a form, our server briefly holds your IP address in memory to stop spam and repeated submissions. It is not stored or used to identify you.
    • Messages and suggestions. Your name, email and what you tell us.

    Why we use it

    We use your information only for the reason you gave it to us: to send the newsletter, reply to an enquiry, offer you paid work, process a donation or run an event. We will not sell your information or share it with anyone for their own marketing.

    Our legal basis

    Under UK data protection law we rely on your consent for the newsletter and the creative register. We rely on our legitimate interests to reply to enquiries and run events, and on contract or legal obligation to process payments and keep financial records.

    Who we share it with

    We use these services to run the website. Each one processes your information only on our instructions.

    • Netlify hosts this website and runs the code that receives form submissions.
    • Resend delivers messages sent through our forms to our inbox (business@studiocanteen.com).
    • Mailchimp stores newsletter sign-ups, sends the newsletter and handles unsubscribes.

    Some of these companies may process data outside the UK. Where they do, they use safeguards recognised by UK data protection law, such as the UK International Data Transfer Addendum. If someone on the creative register is put forward for a job, we share their details with the client only after asking them.

    How long we keep it

    Newsletter details are kept until you unsubscribe. Enquiries are kept for two years. Register details are kept until you ask us to remove them, and we check with everyone on the register every two years. Financial records are kept for six years, as the law requires.

    Cookies

    This site does not use advertising or tracking cookies. If we add analytics or embedded video in future, we will update this notice and ask for your consent before anything loads.

    Your rights

    You can ask to see the information we hold about you, correct it, delete it, or withdraw consent at any time. Every newsletter has an unsubscribe link. To make a request, email business@studiocanteen.com. We will reply within one month.

    Making a complaint

    If you are unhappy with how we have handled your information, please tell us first. You also have the right to complain to the Information Commissioner's Office, the UK regulator for data protection.
